Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

get up verb

also rise, get out of bed, stand up, stand up!, all rise, classroom commands, get up (of several people), stand up together, stand up (all together)

classical

Traupman 35, 38
Traupman 62: ē lectō surgere, to get out of bed
Traupman 34: stand up, surge (cōnsurgite)
Traupman 321

surgō, surgere, surrēxī, surrēctum

verb, third conjugation

get up or rise

Other words

  • cōnsurgō, cōnsurgere, cōnsurrēxī, cōnsurrēctum — rise up, get to one’s feet

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 57: nōn omnīnō cōnsurgere possum, I can’t get up at all; Cic. Sen. 63: cōnsurrēxisse omnēs (Lewis & Short); Traupman 34: stand up, cōnsurgite; Traupman 321: cōnsurgere

    Rising together or rising all the way up, as from a seat or the ground.

  • assurgō (adsurgō), assurgere, assurrēxī, assurrēctum — stand up for someone, rise out of respect

    with the dative of the person, conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 12: an quisquam in cūriam venientī adsurrēxit? (Lewis & Short); Traupman 34: stand up (as a mark of respect), assurge (assurgite)

Examples

  • Surge, Theodōre.

    Get up, Theo.composed

  • Ē lectō surgāmus.

    Let’s get out of bed.composed

  • surge et ambulā

    get up and walk: Dad, lifting the sleeping boy out of bed (Mt 9, 5, in jest)composed

See also wake up, bed.

SourcesLewis & Short: surgo · Dickinson: Latin Core Vocabulary
